sehemu: Part II: Consolidated Fund and Finances of the United Republic
jina: Removal of the Controller and Auditor-General from office
maudhui: (1) Subject to the other provisions of this Article, the Controller and Auditor-General of the United Republic shall vacate office upon attaining the age of sixty years or such other age as may be prescribed by a law enacted by Parliament. (2) The Controller and Auditor-General may be removed from office only for inability to perform the functions of office, whether arising from illness or any other cause, misconduct, or breach of the Public Leadership Code of Ethics law, and shall not be removed except in accordance with subarticle (4). (3) Where the President considers that the question of removing the Controller and Auditor-General requires investigation: (a) the President shall appoint a Special Commission consisting of a Chairman and not fewer than two other members; the Chairman and at least half of the other members shall be persons who are or have been Judges of a High Court or Court of Appeal in a Commonwealth country; and (b) the Commission shall investigate the matter, report the facts to the President and advise whether the Controller and Auditor-General should be removed for inability or misconduct. (4) Where the Commission appointed under subarticle (3) advises the President that the Controller and Auditor-General should be removed from office, the President shall remove him from office. (5) Where the question of removal has been referred to a Commission for investigation, the President may suspend the Controller and Auditor-General and may at any time revoke the suspension; in any event the suspension shall cease if the Commission advises that he should not be removed. (6) A person who is or has been Controller and Auditor-General shall not be appointed to or hold any other office in the service of the Government of the United Republic. (7) This Article shall not apply to a person appointed to act as Controller and Auditor-General.

(3) Where the President considers that the question of removing the Controller and Auditor-General requires investigation: (a) the President shall appoint a Special Commission consisting of a Chairman and not fewer than two other members; the Chairman and at least half of the other members shall be persons who are or have been Judges of a High Court or Court of Appeal in a Commonwealth country; and (b) the Commission shall investigate the matter, report the facts to the President and advise whether the Controller and Auditor-General should be removed for inability or misconduct.
(4) Where the Commission appointed under subarticle (3) advises the President that the Controller and Auditor-General should be removed from office, the President shall remove him from office.

(5) Where the question of removal has been referred to a Commission for investigation, the President may suspend the Controller and Auditor-General and may at any time revoke the suspension; in any event the suspension shall cease if the Commission advises that he should not be removed.
(6) A person who is or has been Controller and Auditor-General shall not be appointed to or hold any other office in the service of the Government of the United Republic.
(7) This Article shall not apply to a person appointed to act as Controller and Auditor-General.
